Hi Chloe,

Quick question as we're scoping an EHR sync integration between HealthSync and a regional hospital (St. Augustine). The sync will push patient demographics, encounter summaries, and discrete vitals to our ingestion endpoint. A few specifics:

- Payload includes name, MRN, DOB, encounter ID, basic vitals, and a short clinician note (free text, often with identifiers).
- We currently batch every 10 minutes and send via HTTPS POST to a configurable endpoint (we can send full payloads or hashed identifiers).

We need to understand if that flow would require Redwood to be covered by a BAA for us to route PHI through your hosted API, or whether there are configuration options (tokenization, routing to Dedicated/Private deployments) that would avoid needing BAA coverage.

Can you confirm:
1) If HealthSync routes raw PHI to Redwood-hosted inference, do we need a BAA?
2) Does Redwood offer an ingestion pattern that allows us to send pseudonymized payloads while still using the hosted models (i.e., tokenization or stable hashing of identifiers)?
3) If the hospital requires a BAA, do you support BAA for hosted customers or would they need Dedicated/Private deployment?

I attached a high-level dataflow and a small sample CSV with redacted events so you can see the shape. Happy to hop on a call.

Thanks,
Samir
Senior Integrations Lead, HealthSync

Hi Samir — thanks for the diagrams and sample. Looping in Vivek (Security/Compliance) and Laura (Customer Success) so we can give a clear recommendation. A few quick answers up-front:

- Short: yes, if HealthSync sends "raw" PHI (identifiers + notes) to any Redwood-hosted inference endpoint and Redwood processes/stores that data, we would need to agree a BAA.

- There are configuration options to reduce scope (pseudonymization or hashing) that may remove the need for BAA, but it depends on whether the downstream artifacts (model outputs, logs, telemetry) could reasonably be re-linked to an individual.

Vivek — can you confirm what controls we would need to declare in a hosted BAA (retention, telemetry redaction, KMS usage, customer-managed keys, etc.) and whether HealthSync's described flow (10-min batches, clinical notes present) is easily mitigated by tokenization?

Samir — once Vivek confirms, Laura and I can draft a minimal MOP (mutual action plan) and a BAA outline. If the hospital requires BAA and insists on physical isolation, we can discuss Dedicated / Private as options.

Hi Samir / Chloe — thanks for the context and the attachments. I reviewed the sample CSV and the dataflow diagram. High-level guidance below; I'll call out items we need to finalize scope.

1) BAA requirement:
- If Redwood will process or persist PHI (patient identifiers, notes) in any of our hosted environments, we must execute a BAA with the data controller (HealthSync or the hospital, depending on contract). Hosted customers *can* be covered by a BAA; we have a standard BAA addendum for hosted plans but it requires a security review and an approved MOP.

2) Hosted vs Dedicated/Private tradeoffs:
- Hosted with BAA: feasible for many customers. Requirements typically include: encrypted-in-transit and at-rest, KMS-managed keys (we can offer customer-provided keys in some regions), strict retention limits (token-level logs pruned within X days), disabled request-level logging for full payloads, and enforceable DLP rules to redact sensitive fields before storage.
- Dedicated/Private: recommended when auditors/hospitals require physical isolation, on-prem storage, or prohibit multi-tenant processing. This reduces our liability surface but increases lead time and cost.

3) Pseudonymization/tokenization:
- Hashing MRN or DOB alone is insufficient if free-text notes contain identifiers. We can accept pseudonymized payloads for inference if: (a) all direct identifiers are removed or tokenized with irreversible salts controlled by HealthSync, and (b) clinical text is sanitized (PHI redaction) before sending.
- Alternatively, HealthSync can send an identifier map kept only on your side and send only stable tokens + de-identified notes to Redwood.

4) Telemetry & outputs:
- Even if input is pseudonymized, model outputs and debug traces must be treated as potential PHI if they can be reidentified. We need commitments on: output retention, whether outputs are logged, and redaction policies.

Action items / info we need from HealthSync to finalize:
- Expected retention window for raw payloads and model outputs (days).
- Whether HealthSync can perform automated PHI redaction prior to sending (we can share a recommended regex/list).
- Whether HealthSync requires customer-managed keys (Y/N).
- Primary data controller on contract (HealthSync or St. Augustine).

If you'd like, we can run a quick technical call and a short red-team review of a sanitized sample to demonstrate how pseudonymization affects model outputs. I'll prepare a hosted-BAA checklist and a Dedicated/Private scoping estimate depending on answers above.

Regards,

Thanks, Vivek — this is helpful and exactly the level of detail our procurement team wants. A couple of quick answers:

- Retention: Hospital requires raw payload retention <= 30 days and model outputs <= 7 days, with options for on-request purge.
- Redaction: We can run automated redaction on names/MRNs and tokenize identifiers with an irreversible HMAC (key managed by HealthSync). Clinical notes may still contain provider or event references; we will try to sanitize but need to understand residual risk.
- Keys: We can support customer-managed keys (would prefer CMK in the cloud KMS).
- Controller: St. Augustine will be the data controller; HealthSync will be a processor.

I'll upload a sanitized sample + SOW to the Drive link you shared and can set up a technical call next week. Also attaching our draft SOW in case that helps with the BAA template.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Samir
